Dose (S)equence (C)omparison Heatmap

Source: R/sc_heatmap.R
sc_heatmap.Rd

Generates a heatmap showing how people are distributed across the combinations of doses received of an ordered dose sequence (e.g. DTP1, DTP2 and DTP3), for each geographic area of residence, using data from the electronic immunization registry (EIR).

Usage

sc_heatmap(
  data.EIR,
  vaccines,
  geo_level = "ADM0",
  show_consistent = TRUE,
  within_ADM1 = NULL,
  birth_cohorts = NULL,
  allow_same_day = FALSE,
  fix_residence = TRUE,
  digits = 0
)

Arguments

data.EIR

Data frame. A data frame containing individual vaccination records. See immunABC.EIR for expected structure.

vaccines

Character. A character vector of at least two doses with the ordered dose sequence to evaluate, e.g. c("DTP1", "DTP2", "DTP3").

geo_level

Character. The geographic level of residence to show as columns. Must be "ADM0", "ADM1" or "ADM2". If not specified, the default is "ADM0".

show_consistent

Logical. Whether to show consistent and DATE_MISSING sequences, with percentages over all people in each area (TRUE, default), or only inconsistent sequences, with percentages over the inconsistent sequences in each area (FALSE).

within_ADM1

Character (optional). This optional character vector lets you specify one or several "ADM1" to filter. Default is NULL, which means no filtering by "ADM1".

birth_cohorts

Numeric (optional). A vector specifying the birth cohort(s) to evaluate. If NULL (default), all available cohorts are used.

allow_same_day

Logical. Whether two consecutive doses administered on the same day are considered chronologically consistent. Default is FALSE, since doses of the same vaccine series should not be administered on the same day.

fix_residence

Logical. When a person's residence differs across their records, whether to correct all of that person's records to the residence of their most recent vaccination (TRUE, default) or leave the data as-is (FALSE), in which case each person is assigned the residence of their first record.

digits

The number of digits to show in the labels. Default is 0.

Value

A ggplot object representing the heatmap.

Details

Rows are split into consistent sequences (no dose skipped and doses in chronological order, e.g. "DTP1", "DTP1 + DTP2", "DTP1 + DTP2 + DTP3"), DATE_MISSING sequences and inconsistent sequences (e.g. "DTP1 + DTP3", or "DTP1 + DTP2 (out of order)" when the doses were not administered in chronological order). By default (show_consistent = TRUE), percentages are calculated over all people with at least one dose of the sequence in each area, so inconsistent sequences can be compared against the consistent ones. Set show_consistent = FALSE to hide consistent and DATE_MISSING sequences and deep dive into the inconsistent ones: percentages are then recalculated over the inconsistent sequences of each area only.

Only people with at least one dose of the sequence are evaluated. Since this is a nominal indicator, each person is assigned to a single place of residence (see fix_residence).
